description: This updated edition of the best-selling Small Engines and Power Equipment is more than a simple engine repair manual. Designed for the beginner with little or no mechanical experience, this book is a graphically appealing, step-by-step guide that covers all of the most important engine maintenance and repair skills you'll need to keep your equipment running at peak performance. It also shows exactly how to perform mechanical upkeep and repairs on the most common outdoor power implements. With new and improved content for today's motorized equipment, this DIY bible includes engine and mechanical repair plus maintenance instruction for all your outdoor power equipment , including lawn mowers, snow blowers, chain saws, power washers, generators, leaf blowers, rototillers, wood splitters, lawn edgers, and weed whips. With clear how-to photos and detailed diagrams , you'll see exactly what needs to be done. A comprehensive troubleshooting guide helps you define problems and enact solutions. Among the many skills you'll learn are seasonal tune-ups, changing oil, servicing spark plugs, cleaning filters, replacing muffler, servicing the fuel tank, overhauling the carburetor, servicing brakes, inspecting flywheels, replacing the fuel pump, and replacing a rewind cord. With Small Engines and Outdoor Power Equipment 2nd Edition in your library, you won't need to haul the lawn mower off to the repair center and wait a few weeks just because a filter is plugged or the old gas needs to be replaced. description: How a Small Engine Works A Clear Guide to Understanding Small Engines and Why They Fail Small engines power the equipment people rely on every day. Lawn mowers, snowblowers, generators, pressure washers, pumps, and utility machines all depend on compact engines designed to deliver reliable power with very few parts. Yet when these engines run poorly or fail, the cause often feels confusing and unpredictable. This book explains what is actually happening inside a small engine, using clear language and real-world examples. It focuses on how fuel, air, ignition, compression, lubrication, cooling, and load interact in simple mechanical systems and why small engines react so quickly when something is wrong. This book teaches understanding. It shows how to read engine behavior, recognize symptoms, and trace problems back to the system involved. Surging, stalling under load, hard starting, overheating, backfiring, and sudden failures are explained logically instead of treated as mysteries. Inside this book you will learn: • How small engines convert fuel into usable motion • Why small engines stall instead of powering through resistance • The real differences between two-stroke and four-stroke engines • How carburetors, governors, and ignition systems actually work • Why air cooling and cleanliness matter so much • How load, shaft orientation, and equipment design affect behavior • How to diagnose problems by symptom rather than guessing • What mistakes commonly shorten engine life This book is written for equipment owners, DIY-minded readers, and anyone who wants a solid understanding of how small engines work. It explains how to perform routine maintenance tasks such as oil changes, spark plug replacements, and air filter cleaning. Illustrations and diagrams throughout the book help clarify complicated concepts, making it accessible for readers with no prior technical experience. description: THE PART YOU REPLACED WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM. It fires on the third pull, runs for ten seconds, then dies. So you clean the carburetor. Then you buy a new carburetor. Then a plug, a filter, a fuel line, a gas cap. $200 of parts later it still will not start , and the mower only cost $250 in the first place. Have you ever fitted a brand new part and had nothing change ? Has a book or a video ever told you to "check the fuel system" and then left you standing there? Do you own the tools and still not know what the reading is supposed to be ? You are not bad at this. Nobody ever gave you the numbers. A small engine will tell you exactly what is wrong in about fifteen minutes, but only if you know what to measure and what a healthy engine reads. That is what this handbook is for. The three tests that find almost every dead engine , spark, fuel and compression, run in the order that rules out the most for the least work. A healthy four-stroke cranks 60 to 90 psi. Below about 40 psi, no carburetor on earth will fix it. Learn to read the gauge before you spend another dollar, including the beginner mistake that makes a good engine read 20 to 30 psi low. Why a spark plug reads black on one machine and white on another , and what each color tells you to do next. Real specification tables : torque in ft-lb and in-lb, spark plug gaps to the thousandth of an inch, armature air gaps, valve clearances, wear limits and fuel mix ratios , taken from manufacturer service documents with the source and the date printed beside every value .
